cohort: 886 pregnant women delivering in 11 hospitals in China were assigned to either a hands-and-knees or supine delivery position group.
finding: Women delivering in the hands-and-knees position experienced lower rates of episiotomy and higher rates of intact perineum or first-degree lacerations, without an increase in neonatal asphyxia or postpartum bleeding.
mod_finding: The hands-and-knees delivery position led to lower rates of episiotomy and more intact perineums compared to the supine position.
